rationale: DisjointClasses(A,B) makes A⊓B empty. C⊑A and C⊑B force C⊑A⊓B, so C is unsatisfiable (C⊑owl:Nothing). The ontology itself stays consistent because no individual is asserted to be in C; A and B are satisfiable (only constrained to be pairwise disjoint). Note C⊑owl:Nothing is also entailed (not asserted here to avoid relying on the bottom-subsumption path).
